title: How to save okra seeds
seoTitle: How to Save Okra Seeds for Next Year
description: Save okra seeds by letting pods dry brown on the plant, then shelling, drying and storing the seeds. When they're ready and how long they last.
summary: Leave a few pods on your healthiest plants until they turn brown and dry. Then shell the seeds, let them dry a little longer, and store them somewhere cool and dry for next season.

heroImage.alt: Three dried, ridged okra pods held up in the garden, one split open to show a row of dark seeds inside.

socialImage.alt: How to save okra seeds card with a photo of dried okra pods split open to show the seeds.

targetQueries: how long do okra seeds last
intro: Okra was Olivia's favorite thing to grow. Her family has kept her plants going by saving seed, and every packet the foundation mails comes from that line. You can do the same with a few of your own plants and almost no equipment.
Don't have okra growing yet? Start with [free okra seeds](/okra/free-okra-seeds) from Olivia's garden.

items: A few healthy plants of one open-pollinated variety, like Clemson Spineless.
Paper envelopes or a glass jar, and a pen for labels.
A cool, dry, dark place for storage.

sections.title: Choose which plants to save seed from

blocks.text: Pick your strongest plants, the ones that grew well and gave you good pods. Choose a few pods on each and stop picking them. A twist tie around the stem helps you remember which ones to leave.
Save seed only from open-pollinated varieties like Clemson Spineless. Their seed grows into the same kind of plant. Seed from hybrid varieties won't come back true.

sections.title: When okra seeds are ready to harvest

blocks.text: Let the saved pods keep growing well past eating size. Over several weeks they turn brown, dry, and papery. They're ready when the seams start to split and the seeds rattle when you shake the pod.

blocks.title: If the weather turns
blocks.text: If frost or a long stretch of rain is coming first, cut the pods with a bit of stem and finish drying them indoors somewhere warm and airy.

items: Split each dry pod along its seams over a bowl and run your thumb down the inside.
Keep the plump, dark seeds and toss any that are small, pale, or shriveled.
Spread the seeds on a paper plate and let them dry for another week or two.

sections.title: How to store okra seeds and how long they last

blocks.text: Put the dry seeds in a paper envelope or a glass jar labeled with the variety and the year. Keep it somewhere cool, dry, and dark, not in a hot garage or a humid shed.

Stored that way, okra seed usually grows well for two to three years. For anything older, fold 10 seeds into a damp paper towel, keep it warm for about a week, and count the sprouts. If 8 come up, plant a little thicker to make up the difference.

Bees can carry pollen between different kinds of okra, so seed saved near another variety may come up as a mix. The simplest fix is to grow just one variety. Seed savers who want to keep a variety pure next to other okra plant anywhere from about 800 feet to half a mile apart.

faq.question: Can you save seeds from store-bought okra?
faq.answer: Usually not. Okra sold for eating is picked young, before its seeds are mature, so they won't sprout. Let pods dry on a growing plant instead.

faq.question: What do I do with all the extra okra seeds?
faq.answer: Share them with friends and neighbors, and add your patch to the [Okra Project map](/okra) so others can see where Olivia's okra is growing.
